title: Indefinite leave to remain (permission to stay as a refugee, humanitarian protection, discretionary or section 67 leave): Overview - GOV.UK

content.p: You may be able to apply for indefinite leave to remain ( ILR ) if you have:

content.li: protection status (permission to stay as a refugee or person with humanitarian protection)

content.p: Indefinite leave to remain is how you settle in the UK. It’s also called ‘settlement’. It gives you the right to live, work and study here for as long as you like, and apply for benefits if you’re eligible. You can use it to apply for British citizenship.
Check if you’re eligible for indefinite leave to remain .
Your family members may also be able to apply.
If you have section 67 leave, you can only include your child in your application. If you want other family members to join you in the UK, you will need to apply for a family visa .

content.h3: Partners and children in the UK

content.p: If they’re already in the UK as your dependant, they can apply to stay in the UK with you if they’re eligible. This includes children born in the UK.
Check if your family member is eligible .
If your application is successful, your family members will usually have permission to stay in the UK for the same length of time as you.

content.h3: Partners and children outside the UK

content.p: Your family members may be able to apply to be reunited with you. They must first apply for a visa to join you in the UK . This also applies if they’re not eligible to apply as your partner or child.

content.h3: If you care for an adult relative

content.p: Your adult dependent relative can apply if all the following are true:

content.li: they have a family visa as an adult dependent relative
you have protection status (permission to stay as a refugee or person with humanitarian protection)

content.p: They must apply separately - you cannot include them on your application.
Make your applications at the same time. Your adult dependent relative’s visa will expire if you’re granted ILR.
There’s no fee if you have protection status (permission to stay as a refugee or person with humanitarian protection) or section 67 leave. This will also apply to your partner or child.

If you have discretionary leave it costs £3,226 for you and each other person you include in your application. You’ll each need to have your biometric information (fingerprints and a photo) taken - there’s no fee for this.
You’ll be told whether your application has been successful within 6 months of when you either:

content.li: submit your application - if you’re told to use the ‘UK Immigration ID Check’ app
have your fingerprints and photo taken - if you’re told to go to a UKVCAS service point

content.p: If you have discretionary leave and you paid to use the ‘super priority service’, you’ll get a decision within 2 working days. Working days are Monday to Friday, not including bank holidays.
You cannot use the ‘super priority service’ if you have protection status (permission to stay as a refugee or person with humanitarian protection) or section 67 leave.
You must not travel outside the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man until you get a decision. Your application will be withdrawn if you do.
You’ll be contacted if your application is complex and will take longer, for example:

content.li: if your supporting documents need to be verified
if you need to attend an interview
because of your personal circumstances, for example if you have a criminal conviction

content.p: You can do the following:

content.li: use public services, such as healthcare and schools
apply for public funds (benefits) and pensions
apply for British citizenship , usually after a minimum of 12 months

content.p: You can travel outside the UK using a Home Office travel document .
You can lose your indefinite leave to remain if you:

content.li: travel back to the country you sought asylum from
stay outside the UK for more than 2 years - you may need to apply before you can return to the UK

content.h2: If your application for indefinite leave to remain is refused

content.p: If you have protection status (permission to stay as a refugee or person with humanitarian protection) or discretionary leave, you might still be able to stay in the UK. Your decision letter will explain what you’ve been offered instead of indefinite leave to remain.
If you have section 67 leave, you will need to apply for another form of leave (for example, a visa) to stay in the UK.
